yeahfluiddynamics:
A very important experiment for fluid dynamics and aviation was performed by Ludwig Prandtl in 1904. In a talk at the third International Congress of Mathematicians in Heidelberg, Germany he described his simple model for the flow of fluids past solids: boundary layers.
Prandtl’s model showed that the frictionless (inviscid) flow far from a solid object is significantly affected by the viscous flow close to the body. In particular, if the boundary layer detaches from the body then the drag force can increase significantly. His explanation was the first mathematical treatment of turbulence.
This was the start of many experiments with flat plates placed in water tanks, wind tunnels, or air. Here you see one of these early setups in the Aerodynamics Research Laboratory of Princeton University. The experiment is similar to what is now known as “the rotating tank.” This type of experiment has been used extensively for studies of boundary layers.
Image source: National Center for Atmospheric Research.

yeah! (a long post on how we came to our baby’s name)
Posted: March 13, 2011 | Author: amandagregoryx | Filed under: Uncategorized | Leave a comment
i think i’ve mentioned here before that naming is an important thing. it was really important for us when we named our first child and i wrote a long post about why we chose her name.
when i found out i was pregnant the second time i thought i could go on the name site and find some sort of magic. you know… there are those tests where you fill out some answers and it gives you your personality or whatever. like how your life is a 9 or a 7 or a 2 (we’re both twos… i’m not sure if this is good). but it just wasn’t working for me. and i’d spent all those months trying to get pregnant and feeling bad that we didn’t have a boy for the baby. and then we finally got pregnant and we found out that the baby would be another girl. which is amazing in itself
